title: The American family isn\x26#39;t collapsing, it\x26#39;s adapting to reality
titleZh: 被生活成本斩杀的美式旧家庭
summary:
当评论员和媒体舆论人士警告美式家庭正在走向衰落时，他们实际所指的往往是：如今的美国家庭形态即便与短短五年前相比也已大不相同。越来越多的美国年轻人将如何维持基本的经济生存放在首位，而将结婚、购房或生育等计划推迟——这并不是出于自私，而是迫于现实。根据Investopedia在2025年发布的一项成本分析，购房、医疗、育儿、教育、养老一系列美式传统人生里程碑，在一个人的一生中累计所需支出已超过500万美元。仅是这个数字本身，就足以解释为什么如此多人感到，实现这些目标的可能性已被剥夺。

来源：USA Today；作者：Andrew Sciallo；原文发布时间：2025-12-30 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: When pundits and media talking heads warn that the American family is in decline, what they’re really saying is that it looks drastically different today than it did even five years ago. More young Americans are prioritizing economic survival over marriage, homeownership or having children – not out of selfishness, but out of necessity. According to a 2025 Investopedia cost analysis, the cumulative price of traditional American milestones – homeownership, health care, childcare, education and retirement – now passes $5 million over a lifetime. That figure alone explains why so many people feel disenfranchised.
paragraphs.contentZh: 当评论员和媒体舆论人士警告美式家庭正在走向衰落时，他们实际所指的往往是：如今的美国家庭形态即便与短短五年前相比也已大不相同。越来越多的美国年轻人将如何维持基本的经济生存放在首位，而将结婚、购房或生育等计划推迟——这并不是出于自私，而是迫于现实。根据Investopedia在2025年发布的一项成本分析，购房、医疗、育儿、教育、养老一系列美式传统人生里程碑，在一个人的一生中累计所需支出已超过500万美元。仅是这个数字本身，就足以解释为什么如此多人感到，实现这些目标的可能性已被剥夺。

paragraphs.contentEn: Research consistently shows that rising housing costs shape family formation. An economic study found that for every 10% increase in home prices, birth rates among non-homeowners dropped by roughly 1%. Demographic research hosted on ResearchGate similarly shows that the lack of affordable housing delays first births and reduces overall fertility. It’s a misnomer to say that Generation Z is abandoning the American dream when in reality, the American dream is abandoning them.
paragraphs.contentZh: 多项研究一致表明，不断上涨的住房成本正在深刻影响人们的成家过程。一项经济学研究发现，房价每上涨10%，未购房人群的生育率便会下降约1%。另一项发布于ResearchGate的人口学研究也指出，缺乏可负担住房不仅推迟了人们的首次生育时间，也拉低了整体生育水平。因此，将这一现象简单归结为Z世代正在放弃美国梦并不准确，更贴近现实的说法是，美国梦正在将他们拒之门外。

paragraphs.contentEn: Nowhere is this more visible than in New York City, where I live and teach. Happy hour bars in Manhattan are packed every evening – not with friends but coworkers. Introductions begin not with "Who are you?" but "What do you do?" Work has come to define identity in America, even though few seem to like the version of themselves it produces. This overemphasis on career success leaves little time or energy for building families or community. That context matters when discussing the recent fixation on “no contact” families. While estrangement is hardly new, it’s now framed as a uniquely Gen Z phenomenon. Why?
paragraphs.contentZh: 这一点在我居住并任教的纽约市体现得尤为明显。曼哈顿的欢乐时光酒吧每晚都座无虚席——但聚在一起的不是朋友，而是同事。人们彼此介绍时，开口问的不再是“你是谁？”，而是“你是做什么工作的？”。在美国，工作已经成为界定个人身份的核心方式，尽管很少有人真心喜欢这个被职业所定义的自己。对事业成功的过度强调，也让人们难以抽出时间和精力去经营家庭、融入社群。在探讨近期备受关注的“断联家庭”现象时，理解这一背景至关重要。家庭成员间的疏离并不是新现象，如今却被包装成一种Z世代独有的问题。何以至此？

paragraphs.contentEn: Recently, media therapist Mel Robbins sparked controversy with a New York Times op-ed arguing that going no contact is a mistake. The backlash was swift, drawing responses from wellness influencers, therapists and younger people who saw her argument as disconnected from economic reality. Younger generations are once again cast as disruptors of tradition – a role once assigned to the baby boomers by the Silent Generation. But what truly reshapes social behavior isn’t feelings; it’s economics. The cost of living has a greater influence on American life than ideology ever has. Even the origins of the holiday season seem to tell this story. Much of America’s holiday mythology emerged during the early 20th century, shaped by events like the Great Depression and both World Wars. At a time when Americans had less, there was a greater emphasis on connection, ritual and shared hardship.
paragraphs.contentZh: 近日，网络心理治疗师梅尔·罗宾斯在《纽约时报》发表专栏文章，称与家人断联是一种错误做法，随即引发广泛争议。反弹迅速而猛烈，来自健康领域的意见领袖、心理治疗师以及不少年轻人发声回应，指责她的论断脱离了当下的经济现实。年轻一代再次被刻画为冲击传统的破坏者——这一角色曾经也被沉默的一代贴在婴儿潮一代身上。然而真正重塑社会行为的，并不是情绪或态度；而是经济因素。生活成本对美国社会的影响，远比任何意识形态都更为深刻。即便追溯节日文化的起源，也能看到相似的逻辑。美国许多节日的文化叙事形成于20世纪初，深受大萧条与两次世界大战的影响。在那个物质更加匮乏的年代，人们反而更加注重彼此之间的联结、生活仪式的构建，以及共度时艰的集体记忆。

paragraphs.contentEn: Today, overconsumption has hollowed out those traditions. A recent survey by the World Happiness Report found that while Americans have more material wealth than most other countries, they have fallen to 24th in the global happiness ranking, their lowest ranking ever. Yet surveys show that more and more Americans are waking up to the reality that overconsumption does not make one happier. And research finds materialism itself is linked to lower well-being. This, even as fewer and fewer Americans report being satisfied with their lives, according to a 2025 Gallup poll. Americans own more than ever, yet they report historically low levels of happiness.
paragraphs.contentZh: 如今，过度消费正在掏空这些传统的内核。《世界幸福报告》近期的一项调查显示，尽管美国人的物质财富水平远高于多数国家，其全球幸福感排名却已下滑至第24位，创该榜单发布以来的最低纪录。同时，多项调查表明，越来越多的美国人开始意识到，过度消费并不会带来更高的幸福感。研究还指出，物质主义本身，就与较低的主观幸福水平密切相关。根据盖洛普2025年的民意调查，表示对生活感到满意的美国人比例仍在持续走低。尽管拥有的物质财富比以往任何时候都多，美国人自我报告的幸福水平却降至历史低点。

paragraphs.contentEn: If there is a silver lining to this economic turmoil, it’s that many Americans are becoming more intentional about how they spend their time. Increasingly, people are asking: What actually makes my life meaningful? What is my version of the American dream? For many, homeownership may be out of reach, but legacy is not. Traveling somewhere new, creating art, building chosen families or simply protecting one’s mental health can be more fulfilling than any material milestone. This is the shift that unsettles older generations: a vision of the American dream untethered from property or possessions, rooted instead in lived experience and personal autonomy.
paragraphs.contentZh: Z世代正在重新审视家庭义务，而“断联”的争议忽略了这一点。

paragraphs.contentEn: The outrage over the no-contact trend is a convenient distraction from a more complex truth: The cost of American life has reached a breaking point. That pressure has strained relationships and has forced difficult choices. Time and emotional energy have become more valuable resources. For some young adults, choosing not to attend a stressful family gathering and opting instead for rest, travel or solitude is not selfish. It’s self-preservation. Family obligations are often the most resented part of American life, yet many continue them out of guilt rather than desire. Some comply and complain. Others quietly opt out. And it’s the latter group – those who choose differently – who are most harshly judged. The American family isn’t collapsing. It’s adapting to an economic reality that leaves little room for the old rules. What looks like decline is, in fact, evolution.
paragraphs.contentZh: 围绕断联趋势的愤怒，更像是一种便利的视线转移，掩盖了更为复杂也更为严峻的现实：美式生活的成本已逼近临界点。这种压力使人际关系持续紧绷，也迫使人们做出艰难抉择。时间与情感精力，已成为越发珍贵的资源。对一些年轻人而言，选择不去参加令人焦虑的家庭聚会，而是把时间留给休息、旅行或独处，并非自私，而是自我保护。在美国社会，家庭义务往往是最容易引发怨气的部分，但许多人仍在履行它，并不是出于意愿，而是源于内疚。有人选择一边顺从、一边抱怨；也有人选择悄然退出。而真正遭受最严厉指责的，恰恰是后者——那些选择不再照旧行事的人。美式家庭并没有走向瓦解，它只是在适应一种几乎不为旧规则留下空间的经济现实。看似是衰退的变化，实际上是一场正在发生的演进。
